## 1. ANABELIAN_SUCCESSOR

### ANABELIAN_SUCCESSOR:A.1

**Claim.** For a proper smooth geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a finite field, equality of two rational-point sections in the full geometrically prime-to-p group is equivalent to the stated p-primary point-difference condition on every pointed prime-to-p Galois cover after every finite constant extension. The compatible lift over each cover is unique.

**Claim.** For genus two and an auxiliary odd prime for which p is primitive, a collision forces the specified constant occupancy congruences in J/ell J. A cyclic quotient with at least twice its kernel-size many points and more cosets than points must satisfy the relative class-number criterion.

**Run status and location.** Proved; INTAKE_A_1_returns/ANABELIAN_SUCCESSOR_final/ANABELIAN_SUCCESSOR_paper.tex, Statement A.10 (starts at line 562).

### ANABELIAN_SUCCESSOR:A.14

**Claim.** For a pointed cyclic prime-to-p cover of odd degree greater than1, rational p-torsion-freeness of its primitive Jacobian factor rules out a collision provided the base is not geometrically a separable double cover of a genus-one curve.

**Run status and location.** Proved; INTAKE_A_1_returns/ANABELIAN_SUCCESSOR_final/ANABELIAN_SUCCESSOR_paper.tex, Statement A.14 (starts at line 731).

**Proof.** yes, proof body read; complete within the stated hypotheses and cited inputs.

**Check.** targeted proof check. holds: the primitive projector would give a separable function of degree2^omega(n) with simple support in two free orbits. Poonen’s controlled-field lemma bounds the genus of the field generated by all translates; its faithful free odd action forces genus1. Each fibre over a zero has at most two points in the two orbits, so the remaining degree is2, producing the excluded double cover. The proof uses rational torsion before passing to the geometric argument.

**Programme and notes.** B8. My independent attempt obtained rationality of each partial_j P/P by rational interpolation and identified the remaining constant-factor issue. It also produced an explicit sharpness construction P=A+sqrt(T)B over C(T,sqrt(T)), at the disjoint d roots of A and d−1 roots of B: the derivatives there are 1/(2T) and0. The printed proof gives an even cleaner complete argument without passing to an algebraic closure of the differential field, and I checked it in full. Call u logarithmic if every partial_j u/u belongs to K=C(T). Distinct classes of such u modulo K* are linearly independent over K: normalize a shortest relation to start with u1, differentiate and subtract (partial_j u1/u1) times the relation. Minimality kills every remaining coefficient, so all partial_j(c_i u_i/u1)=0. Exactness of the constant field puts these ratios in C*, contradicting distinctness. Interpolation at d+1 of the supplied centres expresses P as a sum v_chi P_chi with P_chi in K[Z] of degree at most d. Monicity forces the trivial class to occur with P0 monic of degree d; every other P_chi has degree at most d−1. At each centre only its own logarithmic class can have a nonzero coefficient. At least d of the 2d centres are not roots of P0, so each nontrivial P_chi has at least d roots and vanishes identically. Thus P=P0. No scalar-valued quotient error is allowed in this argument. For meromorphic p-adic germs, embedding into the iterated formal Laurent series field makes common constants exactly L: successively kill all nonzero Laurent exponents using characteristic zero. The provided exponential sharpness example A+exp(T1)B is valid on a sufficiently small p-adic ball, and exp(T1) cannot be rational since a nonzero rational R with R'/R=1 would have no finite zeros/poles and would be constant. The degree-one example Z+exp(T1) gives the same lower-bound failure. My algebraic sqrt(T) example also works for d=1 and gives sharpness in the general differential-field statement. This is a complete elementary derivation plus full proof comparison, without relying on a literature attribution for the lemma.

**Programme and notes.** B8-full-metabelian. I read the complete proof in B8_norm_metabelian.tex and checked each transition, rather than infer the theorem from point continuity. The precise field inputs are actual local norm equivariance, valuation continuity on points over every finite algebraic extension, a stable two-grid Kummer-kernel test, arbitrarily large cyclic local quotients of N, and a scalar logarithmic error lemma. The register invokes B126/128/131/132 for those inputs. I additionally verified them directly in the separately checked B140 r=2 kernel argument and B138 normalization/continuity/scalar-error calculation, so this assessment does not silently treat the other auditor's pending rows as independently checked. There is no circular reconstruction step: the stable-kernel calculation, finite grids, group-cohomology normalization, local quotient and continuity precede and do not use the geometric norm theorem. For a finite Noether projection g of degree d, remove the branch locus and the proper closed images of the finitely many grid fibres. The actual P_t is monic degree d. Transfer of the Y−a Kummer class evaluates as kappa((-1)^d P_t(a)); its torsion sign vanishes rationally. The factorial principal open has Picard0 and geometric units freely generated by its split prime boundary equations h_j, giving xi_a=beta_a+sum lambda_aj kappa(h_j). Normalization at one actual point makes beta_a an explicit class over one finite local M, and the stable grid test makes every P_t equivariant for G_M. Pick a split inverse-function ball for g. A nonzero integral Kummer character on N can be saturated by adjoining the required finite radical within its fixed field; then adjoining mu_p^s to M gives L/M cyclic of degree q=p^s>d+1, with N surjective onto its Galois group. ## 5. SECTION_GHOSTS

### SECTION_GHOSTS:P.1

**Claim.** The actual tripod action has cup and corrected higher Massey obstructions; real sections are classified by real components, but these facts give no integral all-depth converse.

**Run status and location.** Known; sections/part_P_literature.tex; P.1.

**Proof.** yes; yes, relative to named standard inputs.

**Check.** source comparison; proof check; hypothesis check. CONFIRMED

**Novelty and sources.** known obstruction and real-section theorems; explicit application checked. Wickelgren2012 author pp14,21–22,26–27; WickelgrenN2012 §3.11/Cor3.12 pp16–17, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1107.1790; Ellenberg2007 pp1–2, https://www.cecm.sfu.ca/~nbruin/banff2007/ellenberg.pdf; Mochizuki2003 Cor3.13 pp142–143, https://library.slmath.org/books/Book41/files/mochizuki.pdf; WickelgrenReal2014 Thm1.1 p2, https://services.math.duke.edu/~kgw/papers/delta2real.pdf. Searches: supplied exact numbered proof and dependencies; primary sources as specified in report

**Earlier treatment.** parent common earlier-event import; named predecessors checked where specified Agreement: see per-row audit derivation and common earlier events.

**Programme and notes.** P.1. Read Wickelgren’s Proposition7, Theorem19, Remark20 and Propositions24–25, and the n-fold paper §3.11/Corollary3.12. The latter explicitly removes coefficient primes dividing n!, and takes a chosen predecessor as input. This is essential at two and three. Independently, the point (3,−2) has zero cup, so bilinearity gives cup(3,4)=0; the pair (3,4) has none of the ordinary or cusp patterns. Full local Kummer injectivity would force its ordinary coordinate to be3 and its complement to be−2, excluding local ordinarity. The opened Ellenberg notes carry the date6February2007. Mochizuki Corollary3.13 and Wickelgren’s real Theorem1.1 apply to the smooth based tripod, whose three components give sign pairs(−,+),(+,+),(+,−). Their hypotheses are satisfied and they provide precisely the real input used in A.4.

### SECTION_GHOSTS:P.2

**Claim.** Published nongeometric pro-prime constructions concern specified regular primes, fields, and quotients; they do not produce the requested ordinary all-prime section over Q.

**Run status and location.** Known; sections/part_P_literature.tex; P.2.

**Proof.** yes; yes, relative to named standard inputs.

**Check.** source comparison; hypothesis check. CONFIRMED

**Novelty and sources.** known input with scope comparison. Hoshi2010 ThmA/Lem3.2 (downloaded primary); Hoshi–Tsujimura2021 ThmA, Prop1.4, Cor2.5, https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/preprint/file/RIMS1950.pdf; Saïdi2023 condition(*) pp573–574 and ThmA p575, https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/41437. Searches: supplied exact numbered proof and dependencies; primary sources as specified in report

**Earlier treatment.** parent common earlier-event import; named predecessors checked where specified Agreement: see per-row audit derivation and common earlier events.

**Programme and notes.** P.1. Hoshi2010 TheoremA and Lemma3.2 require odd regular p, appropriate covers/proper compactifications, rational points and a finite base extension inside the p-unramified extension. Hoshi–Tsujimura TheoremA(i)/Corollary2.5(i) lifts p-unit pairs over a field containing μ_p; its lifting conclusion is distinct from the flawed geometricity criterion audited in P.3. Saïdi2023 TheoremA is over a p-adic local field, for a proper hyperbolic curve with a point and potentially good reduction, and a quotient satisfying all four parts of condition(*). In particular (*)(iv) requires a nonisomorphism Γ^ell→Δ^ell for some ell≠p; the full pronilpotent geometric quotient does not meet that requirement. The supplied proof retains these restrictions. The smaller-quotient companion paper is absent and is not included in this audit claim.

Steklov's leading-constant omission and residual splitting assertion are false as printed. The needed local conclusion is repaired, while the rational order-seven exclusion is a separate false assertion. SECTIONS_OVER_Q A.20 concerns an untwisted residual representation that retains a quadratic ramification character; it is related to, but not identical with, the general leading-constant correction D.22. The explicit formulas and exact comparison are in the section and Fermat reports.

**Tripod and density literature.** Betts-Kumpitsch-Ludtke proves the stated ordinary S-Selmer result for the model over Z[1/2], with its more general conditional Kim route and finite-support theorem retaining their hypotheses. Li-Ludtke's stated imaginary-quadratic S-empty/one-nonconjugation-fixed-prime cases are additional special cases; they do not prove the full tripod section conjecture over Q. N2 checks the missing local-cusp exclusion in the integral-j family and then uses the known ordinary-adelic recognition theorem. The S={2} parameters are -1,2,1/2; they have the same j=1728 but are not all Q-isomorphic Legendre curves.

Porowski's actual no-CM and density hypotheses are retained. The valid strong-density criterion in Sections D.2 is checked. A potentially density-one set need not meet another potentially positive set as required by the printed Corollary7.11 argument: the split and inert sets of Q(i) exhibit the invalid general inference. This refutes that step, not the corollary's Selmer-cardinality conclusion. Effective prime counts cannot repair an empty intersection.

**N3, without and with its named K-theory input.** For odd ell and S={ell,infinity}, the next obstruction of an actual boundary-matched class-r predecessor lies in (K_(2r)(Z) tensor Z_ell)^(b_(r+1)). Odd r retains precisely the irregular-character alternative; even r retains the corresponding even class-group eigenspace, the Vandiver alternative. The full irregular-pair table for ell<200 and ell=691 was recomputed. A nonzero obstruction group need not obstruct a particular section, and cyclicity is not automatic. On the separately named, unrefereed Mok-Zheng input K_(4m)(Z)=0 for1<=m<=30, the even-r<=60 alternative disappears. This conditional consequence is separate from theorem A.

**N4 and N5.** The arithmetic quotient is proved independently even though its original 120-page manuscript is absent. The affine image is constrained by b mod2=epsilon8(a), not the unrestricted affine product. Equality G_Q=GT remains the kernel equality stated above. In N5 the Witt character calculation gives the printed dimension table; a new full-word calculation gives dim W16=75, bracket rank37 and quotient dimension38 over Q and F17. This is compatible with the mapper's earlier lower bound37, rather than a contradiction. Exact ranks and lower bounds are labelled separately.

**N6 and marked actions.** The old unreferenced assertion that strictness GT<GT0 was already known in print is withdrawn. The supplied later gentle-character proof, its lifting theorem, character independence and exact Ihara/Furusho input have their own fresh audit record. Strictness is not accepted merely from the old attribution. The comparison of the Nakamura-Schneps and Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps actions for zero or one marked point is recorded as its own auxiliary statement and checked at its explicit inner correction; it is not inferred simply from abstract group equality. The full marked tower with more marked points remains a separate compatibility question.

**Automatic invertibility.** Theorems A/E of the supplied monoid note were checked in full at the boundary-homology argument. Duality and hexagon suffice for the full profinite rank-two group. In the general surface statement, all boundary components, unit exponents and a bijective assignment are essential hypotheses. Maps on mixed relative completions, maps preserving only selected cusps and arbitrary arithmetic homomorphisms are not silently covered. The two finite duality-only counterexamples were reconstructed.

### 7.3 Analytic interfaces and the accepted theorem A

The supplied Alpoge input is used as a theorem for every Dirichlet L-function, with the attached PDF and Lean statement/entry files read. This audit does not claim a rebuild of the imported Lean development. No covered step is left conditional on Dirichlet RH.

The exact interfaces are recorded row by row in `RH_LINKS.tsv` and as auxiliary statements in `AUXILIARY_ROWS.tsv`. The new explicit-formula calculation in `cross_analytic_links.md` gives a concrete B(q,x) with |psi(x;q,a)-x/phi(q)|<B(q,x), using theorem A and the opened Bennett-Martin-O'Bryant-Rechnitzer bounds. It gives an effective fixed-progression prime criterion after subtracting an explicit prime-power bound. It does not supply an effective threshold for an unspecified density-zero exceptional set.

J_C-large is a kernel condition on the omitted-prime Tate representation, not a density condition. A progression estimate cannot create that kernel. The finite-field character polynomials, Cartier matrices and exact norms use finite-field cohomology and Weil's theorem; their p-unit values are not determined by the number-field zero theorem A. Dirichlet special values and their divisibility govern N3, but zero locations do not prove Vandiver or integral K-group vanishing.

For the actual CM examples, the exact equations and proof directions are in `sections_rh_links.md`: A.143 has algebraic rank two and a proved central vanishing, A.154 has an algebraic descent/pairing proof, and A.160 obtains central nonvanishing from the proved finite2-infinity Selmer input by Burungale-Tian before using Rubin for full Sha finiteness. The general A.22 elliptic-target criterion still names its actual central nonvanishing hypothesis. It is not a hidden premise of Fermat checkpoint13.

For N4's Kummer layers, Hooley's primitive-root argument needs the stated critical-line assertions for Dedekind zeta functions of Q(b^(1/k1),zeta_k), uniformly in its squarefree parameters. The theorem A assertion about Dirichlet characters does not state this nonabelian Kummer-field theorem. The algebraic quotient itself and qualitative Chebotarev do not depend on that extra analytic assertion. No unaudited later Hecke announcement is used as a replacement.

### 8.3 Important compatible statements

A1 point separation is compatible with the failure of universal nontrivial primitive-zero covers, since the latter is a stronger sufficient mechanism. Rational p-unit witnesses and geometric primitive p-rank zero are different conditions. A finite all-extension minimum at the smallest admissible prime is stronger than a successful larger-prime upper bound. The degree-one convention P1=J_C is retained in the identity-inclusive question.

Global nilpotent lifting is compatible with failure of local matching; finite-coefficient vanishing is compatible with a nonzero continuous derived-limit class; and a fixed finite quotient chosen before a ghost is compatible with failure of every compatible all-quotient construction. N3 requires an actual matched predecessor before its obstruction group applies.

The old AS F.18 tests are superseded by later theorems, while the broad mixed-characteristic classification remains open. Finite derived inertia stages and the lower-central union reconstruct; the union of all derived stages is algebraically closed and does not. A failure of one invariant-lift proof in AS F.41 is compatible with the different complete norm argument of successor B.136.

The old attribution of GT strictness to the literature is false as an attribution. The later explicit character proof is a separate mathematical argument. Mapper N5 lower bounds and the exact higher-weight dimensions are compatible. The false root-field disjointness assertion is repaired by the parity-constrained affine image, without weakening the corrected normalization theorem.

## 9. Hunches as concrete Pro questions

`PROMPT_IDEAS.md` gives each question with its checked supporting rows, its importance for the programme and a first step. It includes the prescribed-point and all-extension witness problems, geometric exponent growth, actual all-level norm compatibility, the mixed-prime cover tower, the full CM normalizer, higher local matching and actual-unit norm selection, the GT arithmetic kernel and relative characters, marked-tower compatibility, exact higher-weight computations and the remaining historical-source qualifications. These are questions, not claims that a promising analogy already supplies a proof.

The gap-work ledger records which approaches were actually tried in this intake and where each stopped. A source file that was not supplied is not declared false, and a bounded unsuccessful computation is not called an all-extension obstruction. The final stopping condition concerns two consecutive hourly Step4 reviews with no gap closed and no step refuted; formatting and new speculative ideas do not count as mathematical movement.
